pr_title: System.Half inline operators to CompareTo method
pr_body:
Try to fix #43117
Looks like CompareTo logic was copied from Double
Firstly, I inlined operators, swapped < and == comparison order and dropped extra NaN-checks . So now there are constantly 2 calls to IsNaN() instead of 2-8 (depending on the situation) in the current version
Maybe it makes sense to cache AreZero() value because in some cases it will be called twice, but it can affect on if's laziness

issue_context.title: Optimize Half.CompareTo
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

There is a same problem as mentioned [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/41296#discussion_r475932460). In the worst case [there](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Half.cs#L386-L410) can be 8 calls to IsNaN() due to two NaN-checks at the beginning of all [operators](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Half.cs#L102-L104)

```C#
 public int CompareTo(Half other)
        {
            if (this < other) 
            {
                return -1;
            }

            if (this > other)
            {
                return 1;
            }

            if (this == other)
            {
                return 0;
            }

            if (IsNaN(this))
            {
                return IsNaN(other) ? 0 : -1;
            }

            Debug.Assert(IsNaN(other));
            return 1;
        }
```

Seems like simple operators inlining should help

review_comments:
With the way the JIT emits branches by default, this is probably less ideal because it will assume one of the inputs is NaN, while NaN is typically an edge case in practice.

It might be beneficial to invert this to be "if neither are nan"
Could you share the before/after disassembly and possible some perf numbers showing this is an improvement?
Yup, I'd like to see this too. I'm curious about how much improvement we'd really see here.

In general I think comparing against NaN is not a common operation, so I would expect that handling the `NaN` case in the end is the right way to go? But, if perf numbers suggest otherwise, I'd be good with this change.
